presets.name: Vector's Defaults
presets.description: Raid detection, running here already. Open it to read every rule, or save your own version.
presets.example: a swarm of fresh accounts posting one line
presets.caveat: A Built-In Anti-Raid Policy: detects raids proactively and alerts you with a list of suspects for quick handling.

dials.label: What these rules do
dials.hint: Every rule that runs here, in order.

dials.label: Sensitivity
dials.hint: How much it takes to trip a rule, and how confident the result is.

rules.label: Many accounts, one line
rules.detail: 3 or more separate accounts posting the same line at the same time. The shape of a raid.

presets.name: Scam Links
presets.description: Blocks link shorteners and redirectors that scams hide behind.
presets.caveat: Only catches the shorteners on the bundled list, plus any domain you add.

dials.label: Also block these domains
dials.hint: One per line. The bundled shortener list is always included.

dials.label: Never flag these domains
dials.hint: Your own links, docs, anything you trust.

rules.label: Link domains
rules.detail: 28 domains blocked, subdomains included. Trips at 1 hit in one message, then 3 hits in the window.

presets.name: No Spam
presets.description: The same message over and over, from one account or many.
presets.caveat: Counts shapes, not words: changing case, punctuation or digits does not help a spammer.

dials.label: Sensitivity
dials.hint: How much it takes to trip a rule, and how confident the result is.

rules.label: Same message repeated
rules.detail: One account posting the same thing over and over inside 30 minutes. Case, punctuation and digits are ignored, so changing them does not help. Trips at 4 hits, then 8 hits.

rules.label: Many accounts, one line
rules.detail: 3 or more separate accounts posting the same line at the same time. The shape of a raid.

presets.name: Word Filter
presets.description: Any list of words you choose, with per-channel exceptions.
presets.example: spoilers, slurs, or a scam phrase
presets.caveat: Whole words by default, so filtering "art" leaves "start" alone.

dials.label: Words to catch
dials.hint: One per line. Use *word* to match inside longer words.

dials.label: Allowed in these channels
dials.hint: The filter ignores these channels entirely.

rules.label: Words
rules.detail: 0 words on the list, matched as whole words unless you wrap them in *. Trips at 1 hit in one message, then 10 hits in the window.

presets.name: Mass Tagging
presets.description: One message that names a crowd, rather than a person.
presets.example: a post tagging twelve people at once
presets.caveat: Counts distinct people per message: pinging one person twenty times reads as one, because it is.

dials.label: Sensitivity
dials.hint: How much it takes to trip a rule, and how confident the result is.

dials.label: Allowed in these channels
dials.hint: Announcement channels where tagging everyone is the point.

rules.label: Mass tagging
rules.detail: How many DISTINCT people one message names. Tagging the same person repeatedly counts once. Trips at 6 hits in one message, then 12 hits in one message.

presets.name: Rate Limit
presets.description: Too many messages too quickly from one account, whatever they say.
presets.caveat: Counts messages, not content: a fast typer in a lively channel can trip it, so preview before enabling.

dials.label: Over how many seconds
dials.hint: The span it counts within. 10 catches a burst; 60 catches a sustained flood.

dials.label: Sensitivity
dials.hint: How much it takes to trip a rule, and how confident the result is.

rules.label: Posting too fast
rules.detail: One account's messages counted over any 10 seconds, whatever they say. Trips at 6 hits in the window, then 12 hits in the window.

presets.name: Start from scratch
presets.description: An empty policy. Name it, add the rules you want, preview before anything runs.
presets.caveat: A policy with no rules catches nothing, and the preview will tell you so.

dials.label: Policy name
dials.hint: What you will see in the list.

dials.label: Rules
dials.hint: Add as many as you like. Any one of them can convict on its own.

rule_kinds.label: Words
rule_kinds.description: Someone posts a word from your list.
rule_kinds.input_hint: One per line. Use *word* to match inside longer words.

rule_kinds.label: Link domains
rule_kinds.description: Someone posts a link to a domain on your list.
rule_kinds.input_hint: One per line. Matches the domain and its subdomains.

rule_kinds.label: Same message repeated
rule_kinds.description: One account posting the same thing over and over inside half an hour. Case, punctuation and digits are ignored, so changing them does not help.

rule_kinds.label: Mass tagging
rule_kinds.description: One message naming a crowd. Counts distinct people, so twenty pings at one person is one person — annoying, but not a raid.

rule_kinds.label: Posting too fast
rule_kinds.description: One account posting faster than a person reasonably types, whatever they are saying. Catches a spammer who varies their text just enough to look different every time.
rule_kinds.input_hint: The span it counts within. 10 catches a burst; 60 catches a sustained flood.

rule_kinds.label: Many accounts, one line
rule_kinds.description: Separate accounts posting the same line at the same time. The shape of a raid.

naddr1qqx8yetvv9uj6er9wd5kwmszyq4aspkf0u.title: Designing relays for privacy first
naddr1qqx8yetvv9uj6er9wd5kwmszyq4aspkf0u.summary: Why every connection in Vector goes through one transport layer, and what failing closed buys you when a network is hostile.
naddr1qqx8yetvv9uj6er9wd5kwmszyq4aspkf0u.author: npub190vqdjtlpcq27xslcveglfmr4ynfwg7gmw86cnun4acakxrdd6gqnp929a
naddr1qqx8yetvv9uj6er9wd5kwmszyq4aspkf0u.text:
Every connection Vector makes goes through **one transport layer**. It decides each egress: direct, a bridge into Tor, or a refusal with no socket and no DNS.

Nothing falls back to direct. A preference not loaded yet refuses, and a kind that is still starting refuses too.
